comparison: Both evaluations find strong support for TPEN blocking Ca2+ oscillations through Zn2+ chelation (C32-C38). OpenEval emphasizes dose-response data and specificity controls, while peer reviewers highlight the robustness across multiple activation methods. Both rate as SUPPORTED with high confidence.

Both evaluations support the developmental phenotype findings (C39-C40) showing TPEN-treated eggs complete meiosis but fail pronuclei formation. OpenEval provides detailed analysis of the selective effect, while peer reviewers accept these as straightforward outcomes without challenge. Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Both evaluations strongly support findings that TPEN blocks Ca2+ oscillations across multiple agonists (C41-C45). OpenEval additionally discusses IP3R1 degradation data (C46-C47), while peer reviewers focus on the universality of the Zn2+ requirement. Both rate as SUPPORTED.

OpenEval R3 includes IP3R1 degradation data (C46-C47) showing TPEN prevents PLC-induced downregulation. Peer R10 accepts these findings without challenge as supporting observations consistent with blocked Ca2+ oscillations. Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Both evaluations strongly support the caged IP3 experiments (C48-C51) demonstrating direct IP3R1 requirement for Zn2+. OpenEval emphasizes the specificity controls with rescue by ZnSO4 but not Mg2+ or Ca2+. Peer reviewers affirm this as solid evidence for direct modulation. Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Both evaluations support the ERp44 control experiments (C52-C53) ruling out this alternative mechanism. OpenEval notes the importance for narrowing the mechanism, while peer reviewers accept without comment as appropriate negative controls. Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Both evaluations support findings that TPEN slows ER Ca2+ leak and increases store content (C54-C57). OpenEval emphasizes thapsigargin and ionomycin data with statistical significance. Peer reviewers affirm this as evidence for IP3R1 functional requirement. Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Both evaluations support D1ER sensor data (C58-C59) showing TPEN causes premature termination of ER Ca2+ depletion. OpenEval treats this as direct evidence of impaired Ca2+ release. Peer reviewers include this in their overall affirmation of IP3R1 gating modulation. Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Major disagreement on dKO mouse model (C60-C62). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, viewing the genetic model as validating the TPEN phenotype. Peer R5 rates as UNCERTAIN, questioning whether modest Zn2+ decrease explains the phenotype and suggesting increased Ca2+ amplitude argues against inhibitory effects.

Both evaluations support ZnPT rescue experiments (C63-C66, with OpenEval also covering C63-C64). OpenEval emphasizes dose-dependent Zn2+ increase and consistency with thimerosal resistance. Peer reviewers treat rescue as solid evidence for Zn2+ requirement. Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Disagreement on excess Zn2+ inhibition (C67-C70). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, viewing data as establishing upper boundary of permissive window. Peer R7 rates as UNCERTAIN, questioning whether low ZnPT concentrations truly cause artifact vs. sustained Ca2+ rise, suggesting inhibitory effects may be speculative.

Both evaluations support D1ER sensor specificity controls (C71-C72) showing the sensor responds to Ca2+ but not Zn2+. OpenEval emphasizes this controls for artifacts in ZnPT interpretation. Peer reviewers accept without challenge as technical validation. Both rate as SUPPORTED.

OpenEval R12 synthesizes the central conclusion about permissive Zn2+ window (C5-C11, C75). Peer R1 strongly supports the basal Zn2+ requirement portion (C5-C6, C32-C38). Both rate the basal requirement as SUPPORTED, though peer evaluation is more focused on TPEN effects specifically.

OpenEval R12 includes the permissive window concept (C11, C75) as part of comprehensive synthesis. Peer R8 explicitly supports this concept, with both reviewers affirming optimal/threshold Zn2+ levels are required. Both rate as SUPPORTED despite questions about excess Zn2+ mechanism.

Strong agreement on mechanistic proposals (C73-C74). Both evaluations rate as UNCERTAIN. OpenEval notes proposals are based on structural knowledge but not directly tested, lacking mutagenesis or binding data. Peer reviewers similarly note excess Zn2+ effects are speculative, though the model is helpful.

OpenEval R14 evaluates background/literature claims (C1-C4, C12-C31) as SUPPORTED with proper citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, as reviewers focused on novel experimental findings rather than assessing background information.
